title: Open a corrugated mailer by pulling its tear strip
instruction: Pull the tear strip all the way off and lift the lid so the book is visible. Leave the book in the mailer.
context: Opening a sealed book mailer requires holding the packed carton steady while pulling the small starter tab through a resistant tear, then lifting the freed cover. The strip lets the recipient open the package without bringing a cutter near the contents.
setup: An unopened 252 × 165 × 50 mm single-wall kraft corrugated book mailer has a 232 × 10 mm reinforced front pull strip, a doubled-paper starter tab and a rear crease hinge. Set it at X 337 mm, Y 10 mm with the strip toward the two arms on a level 747.5 mm high bench. A 148 × 105 × 19 mm paperback lies flat inside. The README gives the packed coordinates and a retail-style carton reference.
scoring: 1.0 for complete strip removal and a lid opening of at least 48° held for 0.4 s with the book inside the upright tray. A gripper may support the lid. 0.6 for complete strip removal without meeting the lift condition, and 0.3 for at least 116 mm of tear short of complete removal, provided the book is inside the upright tray. 0.0 otherwise. Check strip length with a ruler and cover angle with a side recording. The tray must be within 20° of upright and its base within 25 mm of the bench.
reset_notes: Place the same paperback in a fresh unopened easy-open mailer after each physical trial. Close the factory seal fully with its starter tab accessible. The simulated reset uses seed 1415158438.
fidelity: Grippers pinch and pull a native tab against measured-pose tension, and lift the rigid front flap on its contact-driven hinge. The tear threshold, leader stiffness and light crease springback are estimates. The flexible ribbon is represented by a moving tear front and render geometry attached to the native leading piece after detachment.
scores: Scripted demo: 1.0 in 466 actions (23.3 s). No-action control: 0.0 in 600 actions. Full tear with no lift: 0.6.
